rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 (score 396.3) is still the best design. It finishes the oval 20/20 at 1.70 s with max_error 0.016 and zero line-loss events. Its failures are on the s-bend (progress 0.46, max_error 0.064, 1.25 line-loss events) and the slalom (progress 0.09, max_error 0.062). Body width is already at its maximum, so the off-track limit cannot move. Steering oscillation and RMS error are small, so the robot is not ringing; it is pushed outward on sharp alternating bends. Iteration 6 widened the outer sensors to +/-0.04 and fell to 290 (oval 13/20, s-bend progress 0.25), so widening the array is rejected. Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.09, mass 0.5) and iteration 4 (kp 5.5, kd 1.0, speed 1.05) both lost oval reliability, so the turn-rate and gain changes already tried should not be repeated.

Changes from iteration 3, limited to two: (1) kd 0.8 to 1.0 adds damping for the faster response on alternating bends without raising kp, which is the gain change that hurt the oval in iteration 4. (2) All sensors move forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06 m, so the array sees the tape earlier and the controller reacts before the wheels reach the outward drift. Sensor x spacing (1.5 cm, 12 mm footprint, +/-0.03 span), wheel track 0.10, mass 0.6, base_speed 1.2, kp 5.0, ki 0.2 and last_direction line loss are unchanged.

Expected result: the oval holds at 20/20 near 1.7 s, and s-bend progress rises above 0.5 with line-loss events below 1. The sensor move is untested, so if the oval finish rate drops, revert y to 0.05 and keep kd 1.0. Hypotheses: (H1) kd 1.0 reduces the overshoot that pushes the robot off the s-bend; (H2) the forward sensors cut line-loss events on the slalom. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and oval completion_time.
